questiontext.text:

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

First of all, we want to recall the following derivations of functions, which are used during worked solution from one step to another step.

Functions Derivative formulas
\( \sqrt{f} \) \(\displaystyle \frac{f'}{2f}\)
\( \ln f\) \( \displaystyle \frac{f'}{f} \)
\((f + g)' \) \(f' + g'\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{f}{g} \) \(\displaystyle \frac{f'g - g'f}{g^2} \)
\(\alpha f\) \(\alpha f'\)

(a) {@f_1@}

Let’s start with finding \( \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} \). We first partially differentiate both sides with respect to \(x\), treating the variable \(y\) as a constant. We then solve for \( \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} \).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \frac{\partial }{ \partial x} ({@aa*x^3*z^2@}) + \frac{\partial }{ \partial x} ({@bb*x*y^5*z@}) & = & \displaystyle \frac{\partial }{ \partial x} ({@cc*x^2@})+ \frac{\partial }{ \partial x} ({@dd*y^3@}) \qquad \qquad (1) \end{align} \)

But

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \frac{\partial }{ \partial x} ({@aa*x^3*z^2@}) + \frac{\partial }{ \partial x} ({@bb*x*y^5*z@}) & = &({@diff(aa*x^3,x)*z^2@} )+( {@aa*x^3*diff(z^2,z)@} \cdot \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}) + ({@diff(bb*x*y^5,x)*z@})+ ({@bb*x*y^5*diff(z,z)@} \cdot \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} ) \\ & = & \displaystyle \left( {@ta_1b@} \right) \cdot \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} + ({@diff(aa*x^3,x)*z^2@} ) + ({@diff(bb*x*y^5,x)*z@}) \qquad \qquad (2) \end{align} \)

and

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \frac{\partial }{ \partial x} ({@cc*x^2@})+ \frac{\partial }{ \partial x} ({@dd*y^3@}) & = & {@diff(cc*x^2+dd*y^3,x)@} \qquad \qquad (3) \end{align} \)

By replacing the expressions (2) and (3) in (1), we have

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \left( {@ta_1b@} \right) \cdot \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} & = & {@ta_1a@} \\ \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} & = & {@ta_1@} \end{align} \)

Next let’s start with finding \( \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} \). We partially differentiate both sides with respect to \(y\), treating the variable \(x\) as a constant. We then solve for \( \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} \).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \frac{\partial }{ \partial y} ({@aa*x^3*z^2@}) + \displaystyle \frac{\partial }{ \partial y} ({@bb*x*y^5*z@}) & = & \displaystyle \frac{\partial }{ \partial y} ({@cc*x^2@})+ \frac{\partial }{ \partial y} ({@dd*y^3@}) \\ ({@diff(aa*x^3,y)*z^2@} )+ ( {@aa*x^3*diff(z^2,z)@} \cdot \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}) +( {@diff(bb*x*y^5,y)*z@} )+ ( {@bb*x*y^5*diff(z,z)@} \cdot \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} ) & = & ({@diff(cc*x^2+dd*y^3,y)@})\\ \left( {@ta_2b@} \right) \cdot \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} & = & {@ta_2a@} \\ \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} & = & {@ta_2@} \end{align} \)

(b) {@f_2@}

Let’s start with finding \( \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} \) We first differentiate both sides with respect to \(x\). We then solve for \( \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} \).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \frac{\partial }{ \partial x} ({@aa*x^2*sin(bb*y+cc*z)@}) & = & \displaystyle \frac{\partial }{ \partial x} ({@ff+dd*y*cos(ee*z*x)@})\\ \displaystyle ({@diff(aa*x^2,x)*sin(bb*y+cc*z)@} )+({@aa*x^2*diff(sin(bb*y+cc*z),z)@} \cdot \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}) & = & ( {@diff(dd*y,x)*cos(ee*z*x)@} )-({@dd*y@} \cdot \left( {@diff(ee*x,x)*z@})+({@ee*x@} \cdot \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\right) \cdot {@sin(ee*z*x)@})\\ \displaystyle ( {@diff(aa*x^2,x)*sin(bb*y+cc*z)@} )+( {@aa*x^2*diff(sin(bb*y+cc*z),z)@} \cdot \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} )& = & \displaystyle ({@-dd*y*diff(ee*x,x)*z*sin(ee*z*x)@})-({@dd*y*ee*x*sin(ee*z*x)@} \cdot \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial x})\\ \displaystyle \left( {@ta_3b@} \right) \cdot \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} & = & {@ta_3a@} \\ \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} & = & {@ta_3@} \end{align} \)

Next let’s start with finding \( \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} \). We differentiate both sides with respect to \(y\). We then solve for \( \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} \).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \frac{\partial }{ \partial y} ({@aa*x^2*sin(bb*y+cc*z)@}) & = & \displaystyle \frac{\partial }{ \partial y} ({@ff+dd*y*cos(ee*z*x)@})\\ \displaystyle {@diff(aa*x^2,y)*sin(bb*y+cc*z)@} +{@aa*x^2@} \cdot \left( {@bb@}+{@cc@} \cdot \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\right) \cdot {@cos(bb*y+cc*z)@} & = & \displaystyle {@diff(dd*y,y)*cos(ee*z*x)@}-{@dd*y@} \cdot \left( {@diff(ee*x,y)*z@}+{@ee*x@} \cdot \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\right) \cdot {@sin(ee*z*x)@}\\ \displaystyle {@aa*x^2*bb@} \cdot {@cos(bb*y+cc*z)@} +{@aa*x^2*cc*cos(bb*y+cc*z)@} \cdot \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} & = & -{@diff(aa*x^2,y)*sin(bb*y+cc*z)@} + {@diff(dd*y,y)*cos(ee*z*x)@}-{@dd*y*diff(ee*x,y)*z*sin(ee*z*x)@}-{@dd*y*ee*x*sin(ee*z*x)@}\cdot \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\\ \displaystyle \left({@ta_4b@} \right) \cdot \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} & = & {@ta_4a@}\\ \displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} & = & {@ta_4@} \end{align} \)

This question asks students to find the partial derivatives \(\frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial x}}\) and \(\frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial y}}\) for two given functions \(z(x, y)\). The students are required to compute these derivatives and provide their answers. The question provides the functions and guides the students through the steps.
